## About
Put My Stupid Thing Together is Reese Turbin, based on Waukegan Rd in Glenview. Ready To Assemble furniture and other home products are the specialty. Storage sheds, swing sets, weight machines, rowing machines, cardio machines. Picture hanging came later, due to customer demand.
Don't let the name fool you. The clients aren't mechanically challenged or allergic to tools. They're competent people, U. of C. students in Hyde Park, Northwestern students in Evanston. They could do it themselves. They'd rather spend the time on something else.
The website isn't slick and it doesn't ask you about cookies. The work speaks for itself: a 5 rating from 141 Google reviews.

## Services
- RTA (Ready To Assemble) furniture assembly: All major brands, including IKEA, West Elm, Sauder, South Shore, Overstock.com and Lifetime. Bunk beds, entertainment centers, dressers, wardrobes.
- IKEA products: Hemnes, Brimnes, Malm, Besta, Pax, Kallax, Galant, Micke and the rest of the lineup, put together.
- Storage sheds, pergolas, solariums: Outdoor structures put together on your property. One reviewer had a gazebo assembled.
- Weight machines, rowing machines, cardio machines: Home gym gear, put together where it's going to live.
- Hanging services: Pictures, mirrors, TV's, sculptures, storage racks, bulletin boards. Stuff, not people. No charge for small hooks or for adding or replacing frame wire.
- Furniture repair: A sideline courtesy for clients hiring for other work. Low end furniture gets back to functional. No high end antiques. Send pictures first.

## FAQ
Q: What should I send when asking for a quote?
A: The brand name and model number, if at all possible. That lets Reese find the manual and come up with an estimate for time and money.

Q: How soon will I hear back?
A: Messages sent through the contact form get a reply within 48-72 hours.

Q: I left a voicemail. Why no call back?
A: Leave your name. Without it, the call probably won't be returned.

Q: Can you provide proof of insurance?
A: Yes. Proof of insurance or a certificate of insurance can be provided or arranged as needed.

Q: Do you repair antiques?
A: No. Repairs are limited to low end furniture, done as a courtesy for clients hiring for other work.
